source.title: MI-MIDI 2: From Observation to Control with Sparse Autoencoders in Text-to-MIDI Generation

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether observational evidence about SAE features predicts steering in text-to-MIDI generators. It does not audit neuron poles or test neuron explanations in language models, as the claim versions specify.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on SAE-feature descriptions and steering in music generators, but none measures neuron jobs, neuron-level explanation accuracy in language models, or the other version-specific claims. These results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on two text-to-MIDI generators and tests whether observational evidence about SAE features predicts steering. It audits no neuron poles and scores no language-model neuron explanations. It does not examine InceptionV1, architecture effects on neuron interpretability, or neuron-based attribution graphs. It cites Bills et al. (an original source) only as the basis for its detection-style recognition task. Its finding that most feature descriptions do no better than permutation controls concerns SAE features of music models, so it does not test V6 or V7 as stated, which are about language-model neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress that the controls matter because most raw correlations reflect note density and most descriptions match permutation controls. They say the density-adjusted versus raw contrast describes the two selections rather than isolating the adjustment's effect.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs on text-to-MIDI model residual states, characterizes features through musical metrics, programs, and LLM descriptions, then steers decoder directions and measures MIDI outputs. It does not audit neuron poles or apply the neuron-explanation methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different outcomes by observational selection route: instrumentation descriptions exceeded permutation calibration, other description groups generally did not; density-adjusted metric features showed a small positive family-level shift at P90, while raw-correlation features showed none. The density-adjusted shift appeared at P90 and not P50. Synth-lead program presence was tested at P50, P75, and P90 in the replication.

fits_no_version.finding: In text2midi and MIDI-LLM SAE dictionaries, LLM descriptions recognized held-out active excerpts at H = 2.221 of 4. That is no better than permutation-control cards (H = 2.100; difference 0.121 [−0.131, 0.388]), and the reviewer reported a shared pattern for every control card. Only instrumentation descriptions exceeded the controls (+0.692 [0.364, 1.033]).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated descriptions of SAE features in symbolic music generators mostly fail to beat permutation controls on held-out recognition, except for explicitly tokenized attributes such as instrumentation.

fits_no_version.finding: One description-selected synth-lead SAE feature steered program 81 in a prespecified confirmation (14/20 vs 1/20 random) and in a replication (6/10 vs 0/10). Density-adjusted metric features showed a small family-level shift (+0.17 SD [0.02, 0.33]). Raw-correlation, program-frequency and description-rating families showed none.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlled observational evidence identifies some steerable SAE features in text-to-MIDI generators, but most uncontrolled observational evidence does not predict steering.

record.problems: The targeted screens use only eight or ten prompts per feature, with coarse per-feature test resolution; none of the exploratory screens had a primary per-feature rejection at q < 0.05. Each final dictionary is a single training run. The LLM reviewer both writes descriptions and selects held-out examples in the same call, sees instrument names and summary statistics, has no recorded sampling settings, and also rates generated music. The family-level analyses were specified after the screens and depend on the resampling scheme. The study uses symbolic or visual endpoints and reports no listening study. The two models differ in architecture, tokenization, pretraining, and dictionary configuration.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results were omitted. The paper's other metric, program, and feature-level tables are not all cataloged as separate rows; the aggregate outcomes most relevant to observational evidence and steering are recorded above.

untested.parts: Neuron job shares in other language models, dense or MoE, at any scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture, regularization and tool effects on the share of interpretable neurons; vision-model estimates.
Attribution graphs from a model's own neurons without a replacement model.
Whether activating-example explanations of language-model neurons predict where they fire (only SAE features of music models are studied).
Simulation-based scoring of language-model neuron explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation to cites_only. The paper mentions superposition and Bills et al. only in related work and does not discuss the neuron-cleanliness claim. All rows correctly carry versions none. The study's subjects are SAE features, not neurons, and its models are music generators, not language models. The general theme (descriptions overfit activating examples) resembles V6/V7, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron interpretability across language models, architectures, or scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability in vision models, architecture effects, or the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons.
Whether language-model neuron explanations based on activating examples predict neuron firing.
Automated simulation scoring of language-model neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM (786 SAE-feature description cards; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: text2midi: 18-layer decoder, residual width 768; MIDI-LLM: 16-layer decoder, residual width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Claude Sonnet 5 described SAE-feature cards and selected four matching held-out excerpts from eight; the description and selection were produced in the same call.

conditions.value: four active and four matched inactive excerpts; choose four

rows.measure: Mean correct held-out selections H out of four
rows.value: H = 2.221 [2.162, 2.282]; 48 of 786 cards reached H = 4 (random-choice expectation 11.2)
rows.note: This is a music-generator SAE-feature recognition result, not a language-model neuron-explanation score.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM (30 permutation-control SAE-feature cards; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: text2midi: 18-layer decoder, residual width 768; MIDI-LLM: 16-layer decoder, residual width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Feature activations were shuffled across excerpts to form permutation-control cards, then evaluated by the same LLM reviewer.

conditions.value: four active and four matched inactive excerpts; choose four

rows.measure: Mean correct selections H out of four
rows.note: The difference interval includes zero; this is a control for the paper's music-feature task.
rows.check: Control row for the permutation calibration; the real-minus-control difference belongs with r1. Keep as a control and do not treat it as an effect.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM (instrumentation-description SAE-feature cards; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: text2midi: 18-layer decoder, residual width 768; MIDI-LLM: 16-layer decoder, residual width 2048
rows.operation_detail: The LLM reviewer selected held-out excerpts matching its SAE-feature description.
rows.measure: Mean correct held-out selections H out of four
rows.note: Instrumentation cards contributed 21 of the 48 perfect-recognition cards.

rows.subject: text2midi L13 f3340
rows.operation_detail: Added the SAE decoder direction for the synth-lead feature at target P90 during generation.
rows.measure: Outputs containing at least one non-drum program-81 note
rows.baseline: 2 of 20 baseline outputs; 1 of 20 matched-random-direction outputs
rows.value: 14 of 20 feature-direction outputs; lift over random = 65 percentage points [45, 85]; p = 0.000122
rows.uncertainty: Paired-prompt bootstrap 95% interval [45, 85]; exact one-sided p = 0.000122
rows.note: The paper says the confirmation passed all four prespecified criteria.

rows.subject: text2midi L13 f3340
rows.operation_detail: Applied the synth-lead SAE decoder direction at P90 in a replication.
rows.measure: Outputs containing at least one non-drum program-81 note
rows.baseline: 0 of 10 baseline outputs; 0 of 10 matched-random-direction outputs
rows.value: 6 of 10 feature-direction outputs; lift over random = 60 percentage points [30, 90]; p = 0.015625
rows.uncertainty: Paired-prompt bootstrap 95% interval [30, 90]; exact one-sided p = 0.015625
rows.note: The paper reports this as a replication on disjoint prompts.

feature direction versus matched random direction and baseline

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM (27 program-frequency SAE-feature candidates; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: text2midi: 18-layer decoder, residual width 768; MIDI-LLM: 16-layer decoder, residual width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Steered program-frequency-selected SAE directions at P90 and measured whether their target program appeared.

conditions.value: feature direction versus matched random direction

rows.measure: Direction yielding more program-positive outputs across features
rows.value: Feature direction yielded more program-positive outputs for 10 of 27 features and fewer for 10 of 27
rows.note: This aggregate comparison does not establish a consistent increase across the candidate family.
rows.check: Feature direction gave more program-positive outputs than random for 10 of 27 features and fewer for 10; all q = 1.000. That is no effect beyond control, not cannot_determine.

rows.subject: text2midi and MIDI-LLM (12 audit-passing description candidates; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: text2midi: 18-layer decoder, residual width 768; MIDI-LLM: 16-layer decoder, residual width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Blinded LLM reviewer rated generated feature-direction and random-direction outputs against fixed SAE-feature descriptions.
rows.value: +0.167 points [−0.300, 0.700]; p = 0.3125; feature variant chosen in 4/8 directional choices
rows.note: The pooled interval includes zero. The synth-lead feature was rated highest, but without it the primary subset difference was −0.036 [−0.400, 0.291].
rows.check: Rating difference +0.167 [−0.300, 0.700], p = 0.3125; −0.036 without the synth-lead feature. The study calls this no advantage, which fits absent.
